nature-pol-040.q: Why do high-stakes groups tend to win under regulatory capture?
nature-pol-040.a: Because they focus their resources on regulation, while the dispersed public, each with little at stake, does not.

nature-pol-288.q: What does a positive feedback network effect do to the value of a network?
nature-pol-288.a: Each added user raises the value for those already in the network.

nature-pol-002.q: Are food miles a major source of carbon emissions in the trade-versus-local-production debate?
nature-pol-002.a: No: studies find food miles a relatively minor source of carbon emissions.

nature-pol-009.q: What does most-favoured-nation treatment require of a WTO member?
nature-pol-009.a: The best terms it gives any WTO member for a product must be given to all members.

nature-pol-014.q: What drives the growth of the electronic waste trade?
nature-pol-014.a: Fast technological change, falling prices and planned obsolescence.

nature-mkt-138.q: Which four services does Costa Rica's payments-for-ecosystem-services programme pay for?
nature-mkt-138.a: Greenhouse gas mitigation, water services, biodiversity protection and scenic beauty.

nature-mkt-153.a: Loans, bonds, notes and mortgages are all forms of debt, which can be owed by a country, local government, company or individual.

nature-mkt-055.q: What does environmental finance seek to do?
nature-mkt-055.a: Move business resources toward sustainable investments while keeping profits.

nature-mkt-037.q: Who proposed the debt-for-nature swap, and in what year?

nature-mkt-154.q: Why might firms divest, and what is divestment for social goals?
nature-mkt-154.a: Firms divest to focus on core operations, raise cash and so on; social divestment includes campaigns over apartheid South Africa, tobacco, factory farming and fossil fuels.

nature-mkt-058.q: Why is the legitimacy of tied aid disputed?
nature-mkt-058.a: Because the OECD's aid committee has long disputed it and set targets to reduce it; a review found far more contract value was spent in donor countries than the 14% of aid donors reported as tied.

nature-mkt-038.q: What is the difference between a three-party and a bilateral debt-for-nature swap?
nature-mkt-038.a: In a three-party swap an NGO buys debt from commercial banks and passes it to the debtor; in a bilateral swap a creditor country forgives part of another government's debt.

nature-res-274.q: How can a country gain a trade advantage by holding its exchange rate low?
nature-res-274.a: It cheapens the country's exports abroad but raises the price of imports at home.

nature-res-208.q: Is groundwater always a renewable resource?
nature-res-208.a: No: of the groundwater used for farming, 16-33% is non-renewable.

nature-res-219.q: Who developed the idea of quasi-rent, and what happens to it in the long run?
nature-res-219.a: Alfred Marshall; in the long run it is competed away as new capital enters.

nature-res-225.q: Why is unconventional oil costly to produce?
nature-res-225.a: Its many processing steps make production costs extremely high.

nature-res-241.q: Where is a severance tax used, and what do some states do with its revenue?
nature-res-241.a: Where resources are privately owned, as in the United States; some states put the revenue into permanent endowments meant to outlast extraction.

nature-res-251.q: When did the idea of conflict resources emerge?
nature-res-251.a: In the late 1990s, with 'blood diamonds' that financed rebellions in Angola and Sierra Leone.

nature-res-035.q: What is climate change doing to fisheries?
nature-res-035.a: It is shifting where fish live and how productive species are, changing the availability and trade of fish products.

nature-res-060.q: How does optimum sustainable yield compare with maximum sustainable yield in fishing effort?
nature-res-060.a: At optimum sustainable yield marginal revenue equals marginal cost, and it usually means less fishing effort than maximum sustainable yield.

nature-res-034.q: Which kinds of capture fishery are there?
nature-res-034.a: Industrial, small-scale or artisanal, and recreational.

nature-res-026.q: Can marine protected areas still help biodiversity despite displaced fishing effort?
nature-res-026.a: Yes: studies accounting for displacement suggest MPAs can still yield a net biodiversity gain when sensitive species are present.

nature-res-055.q: Why do lucrative crustacean and mollusc fisheries matter for the Marine Trophic Index?
nature-res-055.a: They sit at low trophic levels and so pull the index down.

nature-res-022.q: Who gains and who loses under individual fishing quotas, according to critics?
nature-res-022.a: First recipients get windfall profits, while later entrants must buy or lease the right to fish.

nature-res-046.q: What did the reformed EU Common Fisheries Policy add to deal with discards?
nature-res-046.a: A Landing Obligation, since older quota rules forced fishers to discard over-quota fish.

nature-res-014.q: In the logistic harvesting model, at what population level is maximum harvest reached?
nature-res-014.a: At half of carrying capacity K, where it equals one-fourth of K times the intrinsic growth rate r.

nature-res-092.q: What techniques does forest management use?
nature-res-092.a: Timber extraction, planting and replanting, building forest roads and paths, and preventing fire.

nature-res-112.q: Is an aquifer an underground river or lake?
nature-res-112.a: No: aquifers are porous rock saturated with water.

nature-res-098.q: What did the Kyoto Protocol make mandatory in land use, land-use change and forestry accounting?
nature-res-098.a: Accounting for afforestation, reforestation and deforestation.

nature-res-156.q: How does silviculture differ from forestry?
nature-res-156.a: Silviculture works at the level of the individual stand of trees, whereas forestry is the broader field.

nature-res-137.q: What is the main cause of groundwater depletion?

nature-res-108.q: How does land use change relate to carbon dioxide?
nature-res-108.a: Together with fossil fuel use, it is a major human source of carbon dioxide.
